correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty chains, monotone closure operators are exactly fixed-set ceiling maps; the least-private-point argument proves both directions of the commuting/purity equivalence. Commutation forces the joint composite to be the ceiling onto common fixed points. All admissible marked words decompose uniquely into blocks ending in a common fixed point; each block of m intervening positions has 2^(m+1)-1 words. Coefficients of [z/((1-z)(1-2z))]^k give rank R(n,k); summing gives rational OGF z/(1-4z+2z^2), closed form and asymptotic. Finite-meet preservation and extensivity show nuclei on products decouple coordinatewise. Independent brute enumerations checked all 349525 ordered pairs on n<=10, 55 rank coefficients, complete classification of all maps n<=5, and small products. Computation is corroborative, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The well-motivated compatibility problem asks when two intuitionistic-modal closure operators can be composed without order-dependence and what joint quotient they produce. General theory notes nonclosure under composition, but does not quantify finite-chain compatibility. The result gives a complete structural iff criterion, every composite-image rank multiplicity for every chain size, exact exponential rarity, and multiplicativity for natural product-algebra semantics. This is not merely a few small computed values or a renaming of OEIS; the known sequence is explicitly credited.
